text: This is a different "statistics" than SET STATISTICS TIME/IO. Column and index statistics are stored summaries of value distribution the optimizer reads before building a plan, for every query, until updated.

Cardinality estimates come from statistics, not an actual row count. If the real distribution shifts and statistics haven't caught up, the optimizer confidently picks the wrong shape of plan, not just a slower one.

Auto-update fires only after a threshold of changes accumulates, so queries can run on stale stats before it triggers — and ASYNC mode means even the triggering query runs on old numbers. Update manually with FULLSCAN before a known bulk load.
DBCC SHOW_STATISTICS WITH STAT_HEADER is the fastest way to confirm a bad plan is a statistics problem. Next up: DBCC CHECKDB, and the real integrity check statistics can't give you.
